errors: Says runSender 'claims deliveries under a lease with alert_claim (alert_channels.sql:203)'. The sender Worker passes deps.channels (sender/worker.ts:31), so runSender calls alert_claim_channels for every kind, email included (src/lib/alerts/sender.ts:392). alert_claim is the legacy email/Telegram-only claim (alert_channels.sql:1-2,219) used only by the app's deliverNow, whose senderDeps has no channels (src/lib/alerts/standalone.ts:32-42).

Reverses the claim split: 'Telegram, Slack and webhook alerts take the same route ... with their own claim and prepare functions (alert_claim_channels, ...)'. alert_claim_channels is the Worker's single claim for all kinds; only alert_prepare_webhook is webhook-specific (alert_channels.sql:343-349).

Step 4 says the observing probe's store writes the transition and incident. Only the monitor's home probe writes: a non-home probe puts the outcome in its outbox and sends it once a second over signed POST /report (probe/runtime.ts:605-638); the home's Store.apply locks the row and steps the reducer (probe/store.ts:303-415). The hand-off step is missing, so the flow as described is wrong for most monitors.
Trivial citation: deploying.md:14 does not say 'most of the logic lives here as SQL functions and triggers'.

errors: Recommends teamsUrl 'refuse query strings and other tricks, the same way discordUrl'. Teams Workflows (Power Automate/Logic Apps) webhook URLs carry required query parameters (api-version, sp, sv, sig), so this validator would reject every real URL. The answer flags Microsoft's hosts and format as unverified, but states the query-string rule as the design.
